dm: The Eight Types of Noble Beings
gm: The Eight Stages of Entering and Abiding

dm: Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: Does a stream-enterer think, "I have attained the fruit of a stream-enterer"?
gm: Does a Stream-Enterer think, 'I have obtained the fruit of a Stream-Enterer'?

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not so."
gm: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, that is not so.

dm: Why is that? Blessed One, it is because he has not entered into anything at all.
gm: Why is that? Blessed One, because he has not entered into anything;

dm: Therefore, he is called a "stream-enterer."
gm: therefore he is called a Stream-Enterer.

bo: གཟུགས་ལ་ཡང་མ་ཞུགས། སྒྲ་ལ་ཡང་མ་ལགས། དྲི་ལ་ཡང་མ་ལགས། རོ་ལ་ཡང་མ་ལགས། རེག་བྱ་ལ་ཡང་མ་ལགས། ཆོས་རྣམས་ལ་ཡང་མ་ཞུགས་ཏེ།
dm: He has not entered into forms, nor has he entered into sounds, nor has he entered into odors, nor has he entered into tastes, nor has he entered into tangibles, nor has he entered into mental phenomena.
gm: He has not entered into forms, nor into sounds, nor into smells, nor into tastes, nor into tangible objects, nor into dharmas;

dm: Therefore, he is called a "stream-enterer."
gm: therefore he is called a Stream-Enterer.

dm: Why is that? Blessed One, if a stream-enterer were to think, "I have attained the fruit of a stream-enterer," that itself would be his grasping at a self.
gm: Why is that? Blessed One, if a Stream-Enterer were to think, 'I have obtained the fruit of a Stream-Enterer', that itself would be his grasping at a self.

dm: It would be grasping at a sentient being, grasping at a life force, and grasping at a person.
gm: It would be grasping at a living being, grasping at a life, and grasping at a person.

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: Does a once-returner think, 'I have attained the fruit of a once-returner'?"
gm: Does a Once-Returner think, 'I have obtained the fruit of a Once-Returner'?

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not so."
gm: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, that is not so.

dm: Why is that? It is because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that has entered into the state of being a once-returner.
gm: Why is that? Because there is no dharma whatsoever that has entered into the state of a Once-Returner;

dm: Therefore, it is called a "once-returner."
gm: therefore he is called a Once-Returner.

dm: Blessed One, if a once-returner were to think, "I have attained the fruit of a once-returner," that itself would be his grasping at a self.
gm: Blessed One, if a Once-Returner were to think, 'I have obtained the fruit of a Once-Returner', that itself would be his grasping at a self.

dm: It would be grasping at a sentient being, grasping at a life-force, and grasping at a person.
gm: It would be grasping at a living being, grasping at a life, and grasping at a person.

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: Does a non-returner think, 'I have attained the fruit of a non-returner'?"
gm: Does a Non-Returner think, 'I have obtained the fruit of a Non-Returner'?

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not."
gm: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, that is not so.

dm: Why is that? Because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that has entered into the state of a non-returner.
gm: Why is that? Because there is no dharma whatsoever that has entered into the state of a Non-Returner;

dm: Therefore, it is called a non-returner.
gm: therefore he is called a Non-Returner.

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: Does an arhat think, 'I have attained the state of an arhat'?"
gm: Does an Arhat think, 'I have obtained Arhatship'?

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not."
gm: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, that is not so.

dm: Why is that? It is because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that can be called an arhat.
gm: Why is that? Because there is no dharma whatsoever that is called an Arhat.

dm: Blessed One, if an arhat were to think, 'I have attained the state of an arhat,' that itself would be his grasping at a self.
gm: Blessed One, if an Arhat were to think, 'I have obtained Arhatship,' that itself would be his grasping at a self,

dm: It would be grasping at a sentient being, grasping at a life force, and grasping at a person.
gm: grasping at a sentient being, grasping at a life, and grasping at a person.

dm: Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Complete Buddha has declared me to be the foremost of those who dwell in the state of being without defilement.
gm: Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly and fully awakened Buddha has declared me to be the foremost of those who dwell without afflictions.

dm: Blessed One, although I am an arhat who is free from desire, Blessed One, I do not think to myself that I am an arhat.
gm: Blessed One, although I am an Arhat free from desire, Blessed One, I do not think, 'I am an Arhat.'

dm: Blessed One, if I were to think that I had attained the state of an arhat, the Tathāgata would not have declared of me, "The son of good family, Subhūti, is the foremost of those who dwell in the state of being without defilement."
gm: Blessed One, if I were to think, 'I have obtained Arhatship,' the Tathāgata would not have declared of me, 'The son of noble family Subhūti is the foremost of those who dwell without afflictions;

dm: Because I do not abide in anything whatsoever, I do not declare myself to be one who dwells in the state of being without defilement.
gm: and because he dwells nowhere, he is called a dweller without afflictions.'

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: Do you think that there is any dharma that the Tathāgata obtained from the Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Complete Buddha Dīpaṃkara?"
gm: Do you think there is any Dharma that the Tathāgata received from the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly and fully awakened Buddha Dīpaṃkara?

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not."
gm: Subhūti said: Blessed One, that is not so.

dm: There is not any dharma whatsoever that the Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Complete Buddha Dīpaṃkara obtained from the Tathāgata."
gm: There is absolutely no Dharma that the Tathāgata received from the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly and fully awakened Buddha Dīpaṃkara.

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, if any bodhisattva were to say, 'I shall accomplish the adornment of the buddha-fields,' he would be speaking untruthfully."
gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, if any bodhisattva were to say, 'I will accomplish the array of the fields,' they would be speaking falsely.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, the so-called "adornment of the buddha-fields" is spoken of by the Tathāgata as a non-adornment, because those adornments do not exist.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, as for what is called 'the array of the fields, the array of the fields,' it is because the Tathāgata has taught them as being no array;

dm: Therefore, it is called "adornment of the buddha-fields."
gm: therefore, they are called 'the array of the fields.'

dm: Subhūti, because of that, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should generate the mind in such a way that it does not abide.
gm: Therefore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva, a great being, should produce the mind without dwelling in this way;

dm: One should generate the mind without abiding in anything at all.
gm: they should produce the mind without dwelling on anything whatsoever.
